main_text.p: ne circumspicias speciem alienam ).i. curiosé ornatam fœminam non inspicias, ne affectu inhonesto alliciaris: limosi.n. sunt oculi, cito adhæret eis species mulieris. A minimis peccatis prudenter abstinere iubet, ne paulatim incidamus in maiora, Eccles. 19. Psal.127. Ideo etiam Christus monet Matt.5. (ubi præceptum de adulterio exponit) & dicit: Quod si oculus tuus dexter obstaculo tibi fuerit, erue illum, &c. At quod de scortatione & adulterio dicitur, in aliis quoq; peccatis locum habet: neque alius sensus est ad mouendos affectus efficacior, quàm visus, si ei vel modicum indulgeas. ut enim lupus visa oue in rabiem accenditur, sic auarum peI cuniæ & opum conspectus, invidum alienæ felicitatis splendor, iratundum hostis visus commouet, ut abrupto rationis fræno in sceJlus ruant. Et Plato hanc vim oculorum ad amandum significauit, quum sapientiam dixit, si oculis cerneretur, mirabiles sui amores excitaturam.

Propter speciem mulieris multi periérut, & ex hoc concupiscentia quasi ignis exardescit) Sola naturali pulchritudine, & humani corporis corrupta libidine satis provocat mulier viri appetitum, ut Sara, Genes.12. Susanna, Dan.13. Bethsaba, 2. Reg. 11. ideo decori ingenito superaddere fucum, vestiumque ornatum, prorsus iniquum & insolens est. Ideo Petrus præcipit 1. Pet.3. Quarum ornatus sit non externus, qui situs est in plicatura

page.notes: Long s was printed as f and was read as s throughout. "naturali'pulchritudine" has a stray mark between the two words, read as a space. "periérut" carries an accent that may be a printing mark, uncertain. The "11." after "2. Reg." is hard to read and may be "11." or another number. The "Dan.13." and "2. Reg." numbers are small and slightly uncertain. "oue" in "visa oue" is kept as printed. The stray dot before "catis" at the start of a line is not transcribed.
